quest.title: The Moon Adorning the Night
quest.description: The Damselette seems to have something she wants to do in the Silvermoon Hall...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, where's Columbina? Paimon doesn't see her anywhere...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Over here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! What are you doing all the way up there?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Come join me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are we getting ourselves into this time...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you remember those stones we went out to gather last time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Last time? Oh, you mean the ore that glows after absorbing kuuvahki?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Correct. Well, after that, the kuuhenki gathered some more, and I sorted them into two types — darker ones and lighter ones.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Darker ones and lighter ones? But... Why?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: To play Moon Chess, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... What's "Moon Chess"?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh, you've never played?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Nope.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I see... Ever since seeing the grids the children of the Frostmoon Scions draw on the ground, I've always wanted to try it out. But I've never had anyone to play it with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, what are the rules?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hm... It'll be easier if I just show you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Th—That's amazing! How did you do that?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hm? With a little kuuvahki, of course... You can't do that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Maybe you should lower your expectations. We're not all moon goddesses...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: As you wish. Now, this is the board — it represents the "night sky." And the pieces each player controls represent the "moons."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The two players take turns placing their moons in the sky, and the first to get three moons in a row wins.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh! So it's basically a version of tic-tac-toe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, it's called "Moon Chess" here in Nod-Krai, huh... Talk about giving it a local touch...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I see. Well, in this version, the moons rotate, meaning there can never be more than three moons in the sky at once.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: So, when the night sky is full, the moon that rose earliest will vanish.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That... actually makes a lot of sense... and it makes the game a lot harder too!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: So, would you like to give it a try? It'll be my first time playing too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like she's really looking forward to this...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe, sounds fun! Paimon will be the referee! {NICKNAME}'s a clever one, though, so watch out!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Alright then.

talks.objective: Play Moon Chess with The Damselette

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Perhaps... Like this?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Moons... Moons...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: How about here?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Looks like I won this round.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My three moons are connected.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mm, this should win it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mm... The moons wax and wane in an endless cycle...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It seems both sets of moons refuse to be eclipsed.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Are we... heading for a tie?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ah, you weigh your decisions carefully before making them, I see. Take your time — we have plenty of that, after all.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Did you forget how to place your moons in the night sky? Shall I help you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You don't like this game? Hm... I find it quite amusing myself.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mm? Are you staring at me? Your gaze is not subtle.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You're staring... Is the truth of the moons written on my face?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The board's over there, by the way...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hm, your moons are aligned.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The night sky is yours.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ah... I must have... slipped up somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You have a wonderful time playing the game with Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Thank you, I enjoyed that a lot.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If you'd like... feel free to come keep me company again, sometime.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Here, take this as a token of our promise.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The three moons...
